sections.h2: Karnataka grows roughly 69% of India's coffee; Kerala is a distant second

chart.title: Karnataka's 256,695 tonnes dwarfs Kerala's 80,350 in the 2025-26 final estimate
chart.source: Coffee Board of India, 2025-26 final estimate.

sections.means: Karnataka's 256,695 tonnes is roughly 69% of India's 373,000-tonne final 2025-26 estimate.
sections.todo: Watch the Karnataka monsoon first, since analysts flag a weak June there as the main risk to the 2026-27 crop.

sections.h2: Instant coffee and extracts are about a third of India's coffee export value

chart.title: Instant coffee earned $735.87mn in FY26, against $1,405.85mn for beans
chart.source: DGCI&S trade series, FY26, as analysed in the post.

sections.means: Instant coffee and extracts are about a third of export value, so raw beans are not the whole story.
sections.todo: Track the instant-coffee share of exports year over year, since the blog's own trade data can show the trend.

sections.h2: Labour is 65–70% of India's coffee production cost, against about 25% in Brazil

chart.title: Labour's share of production cost is the widest structural gap with Brazil
chart.sub: Labour as a share of coffee production cost, %.
chart.source: Figures as cited in the post.

sections.means: Labour is the cost gap most often cited against Brazil, at roughly 65–70% of Indian production cost against about 25%.
sections.todo: Watch rural labour supply, since the post says rural-to-urban migration is tightening it further.
